(Updates with index/price moves and company news from the first paragraph.)

US equity indexes rose as a rally in SpaceX (SPCX) and Super Micro Computer's (SMCI) shares boosted risk sentiment in growth sectors ahead of quarterly results from Meta Platforms (META) and Tesla (TSLA) post-bell Wednesday.

The Nasdaq Composite advanced 1.1% to 26,701.7, the S&P 500 climbed 0.6% to 7,754.6, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average edged up 0.5% to 52,765.7 ahead of the close.

Six of the top 10 stocks in a category with market capitalization exceeding $200 billion were from the technology sector, according to data compiled by Finviz. SpaceX topped this list of mega-caps, gaining 7.1%. The iShares PHLX Semiconductor Exchange Traded Fund, with about $48.43 billion in assets under management, jumped 1.9% as investors continued to dip their toes back in the AI trade after last week's sharp sell-off.

SpaceX, which also led Nasdaq's gainers, said late Tuesday it swung into the black in Q3 as revenue rose, driven by strong gains in its artificial intelligence and connectivity divisions. Meanwhile, Elon Musk, who heads both SpaceX and Tesla, said the duo has formed special committees to evaluate a potential merger.

A deal could allow SpaceX and Tesla to share technology, reduce overlapping costs and accelerate development, Saxo Bank said in a note Wednesday. The brokerage estimated the companies' combined market value at around $3.5 trillion.

Super Micro Computer's shares surged 9.5% after the company reported preliminary fiscal Q1 revenue and margin results above expectations late Tuesday.

title: Could Starbucks Stock Survive A Sales Slowdown?
detail:
Could Starbucks Stock Survive A Sales Slowdown?
Trefis Team

MCD
QSR
BROS
Explore stocks on Coinbase

For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Over the past year, Starbucks (SBUX) shares returned 19.4%, compared with 17.1% for the S&P 500. After U.S. comparable store sales grew 7.9% in fiscal Q3, management expects growth of 6.5% or better in fiscal Q4 2026. On the July 29 call, one question was how long that momentum can last. If sales growth stalled, would Starbucks' cash still cover its dividend and its debt?

Does Starbucks' Cash Still Cover Its Dividend?

Starbucks currently generates enough free cash flow to cover its dividend, with room left over. In the four fiscal quarters to June 28, 2026, free cash flow was $3.64 billion, compared with $2.81 billion paid out in dividends.

The picture looked different when sales barely grew. Revenue rose just 0.6% in the four fiscal quarters to June 29, 2025. Free cash flow came to $2.25 billion that year, compared with $2.72 billion of dividends. During that slower year, Starbucks paid out about $0.47 billion more in dividends than its free cash flow brought in. A shortfall of that size remains small next to the $3.61 billion of cash and short-term investments Starbucks held on June 28, 2026.

Starbucks Has Cut Its Debt Since Last Year

Starbucks carries less debt today than it did a year ago. Management said on the July 29 call that the company used part of the proceeds from its China transaction to repay about $1.8 billion of debt. Total debt stood at $22.4 billion on June 28, 2026, down from $27.9 billion a year earlier.

Interest also makes a small claim on Starbucks' profit. Operating income was 7.0 times interest expense over the past four fiscal quarters, so profit could fall a long way before interest became hard to pay. Management said the repayment lets the company keep investing in the business and maintain its dividend.

Shareholders Are Paying For Profit Like Fiscal Q3's

For shareholders, the stock price is more exposed to a stall than the cash is. At the October 20 close, Starbucks stock traded at 57.1 times its trailing twelve-month earnings, compared with 23.0 for the S&P 500.

Fiscal Q3 2026 alone produced $1.05 billion of net income, more than half of the $1.98 billion earned over the past four quarters, but about $0.31 billion of that was non-operating other income. Leaving out unusual items, the quarter earned about $0.87 billion. Multiplied by four, which represents what Starbucks would earn in a year if that quarter simply repeated, that profit puts the stock at about 32 times. Buyers appear to be paying for profit like that quarter's to last, and a stall in sales growth would put that expectation in doubt.

title: Warren Buffett's Latest Warning Is Sending Shockwaves Through Wall Street. Here's What History Says Could Happen Next.
detail:
Warren Buffett's Latest Warning Is Sending Shockwaves Through Wall Street. Here's What History Says Could Happen Next.
Will Ebiefung, The Motley Fool

NVDA

Warren Buffett is one of the most successful investors of all time. And over the past six decades, his Berkshire Hathaway portfolio has trounced the market, returning an average compound annual return of 19.7% compared to the S&P 500 index's average of 10.5%.

With such an amazing track record, people tend to listen to what he has to say. High-quality advice is more valuable than ever as the stock market grapples with challenges ranging from high corporate valuations, rising inflation, and political uncertainty.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Let's discuss several recent warnings Buffett has given and decide what it could mean for your portfolio.

Buffett decries a "gambling mood" in the market

Warren Buffett is famous for focusing on value stocks, which are generally shares in companies that trade for affordable prices compared to their earnings and growth. However, these diamonds in the rough are getting harder to find. In a May interview with CNBC, Buffett criticized a "gambling mood" in the stock market and raised concerns about equity prices.

It isn't hard to see why he is getting worried. The cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings (CAPE) ratio is a valuation tool designed to help investors analyze the S&P 500's valuation from a long-term perspective. Right now, it stands at 40.7. That's well above its average of 17.4 and a level that has only been exceeded during the dot-com bubble when it hit an all-time high of 44 in late 1999 before a big crash.

Many on Wall Street now fear that the generative AI boom could be poised for a similar correction.

Buffett's also has concerns about America's fiscal situation

Unlike more outspoken business leaders like Elon Musk, Warren Buffett has typically avoided inserting himself directly into politics -- and wisely so. That said, the situation may be becoming too alarming to ignore. And in his final meeting as Berkshire Hathaway CEO in May 2025, Buffett had some very blunt words to say about the US fiscal situation.

"We wouldn't want to be owning anything that we thought was in a currency that was really going to hell, and that's the big thing we worry about with the United States currency. We're operating at a fiscal deficit now that is unsustainable over a very long period of time."

Image source: Getty Images.

A little over a year and a half later, and the situation he was warning about has become significantly worse. The Trump administration maintained its aggressive tariff policy, and the war in Iran has caused Brent Crude prices to spike 80% since the start of the year. September inflation has jumped to 3.7%, well above the Federal Reserve's long-running target of 2%.

Chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG) stock lost 29.2% in the year to October 20, 2026, while the S&P 500 returned 17.1%. Investors buying today pay 26.7 times earnings, compared to an average of 45.2 at the stock's last 12 fiscal quarter ends. Shareholders who sat through the decline and buyers who waited for it both want to know what the business can still add. So what would a share bought at today's price be worth three years from now?

Chipotle Stock Could Gain About 10% In Three Years

Under these assumptions, a Chipotle share would be worth about $32.65 three years after the October 20 close, 10.1% above today's price. The scenario assumes revenue will grow at 0.8 times Chipotle's latest yearly growth rate. It also sets the year-three net margin between today's level and its recent average, keeping it closer to today's figure. The table below compares today's numbers against the scenario.

Higher revenue drives the gain, adding about 19% as Chipotle sells more food across its restaurants. A slightly wider net margin adds about 4%. A lower P/E takes back about 11%.

When Chipotle Mexican Grill is a large share of what you own, your plan depends on the business delivering more. See how to protect a concentrated position.

Where Would Chipotle's Extra Sales Come From?

Chipotle adds sales in two ways: opening new restaurants and selling more food at the locations it already runs. In fiscal Q2 2026, sales grew 9.3% from a year earlier. Comparable restaurant sales, which track locations open long enough to compare, rose 2.2%.

Restaurant openings are holding steady. Management still expects to open about 350 restaurants in fiscal 2026, the same pace it gave in April. Management said on the fiscal Q2 2026 call that new restaurants still earn cash-on-cash returns of around 60% in their second year.

Sales at existing restaurants represent the slower part of the business. Management, which gave no revenue forecast for fiscal 2026, expects comparable sales growth in the low single digits for the year and around 1% in fiscal Q3. Management also said sales trends softened by about 200 basis points in late July, around the cyclospora issue affecting the industry.

title: Adobe (ADBE): Buy, Sell, or Hold Post Q3 Earnings?
detail:
Adobe (ADBE): Buy, Sell, or Hold Post Q3 Earnings?
Jabin Bastian
Wed, October 21, 2026 at 12:02 PM MST 3 min read
ADBE
^GSPC
Trade Adobe on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Adobe (ADBE): Buy, Sell, or Hold Post Q3 Earnings?

Since April 2026, Adobe has been in a holding pattern, posting a small return of 3.1% while floating around $254.84. The stock also fell short of the S&P 500's 8.9% gain during that period.

Is now the time to buy Adobe, or should you be careful about including it in your portfolio? See what our analysts have to say in our full research report, it's free.

Why Is Adobe Not Exciting?

We're cautious about Adobe. Here are three reasons why there are better opportunities than ADBE, plus one stock we'd rather own.

1. Weak Billings Point to Soft Demand

Billings is a non-GAAP metric that is often called "cash revenue" because it shows how much money the company has collected from customers in a certain period. This is different from revenue, which must be recognized in pieces over the length of a contract.

Adobe's billings came in at $6.71 billion in Q3, and over the last four quarters, its year-on-year growth averaged 11.9%. This performance was underwhelming and suggests that increasing competition is causing challenges in acquiring/retaining customers.

Adobe Billings
2. Projected Revenue Growth Is Slim

Forecasted revenues by Wall Street analysts signal a company's potential. Predictions may not always be accurate, but accelerating growth typically boosts valuation multiples and stock prices while slowing growth does the opposite.

Over the next 12 months, sell-side analysts expect Adobe's revenue to rise by 9.3%, a slight deceleration versus its 11.5% annualized growth for the past five years. This projection doesn't excite us and indicates its products and services will face some demand challenges.

3. Operating Margin in Limbo

While many software businesses point investors to their adjusted profits, which exclude stock-based compensation (SBC), we prefer GAAP operating margin because SBC is a legitimate expense used to attract and retain talent. This is one of the best measures of profitability because it shows how much money a company takes home after developing, marketing, and selling its products.

Analyzing the trend in its profitability, Adobe's operating margin might have fluctuated slightly but has generally stayed the same over the last two years. This raises questions about the company's expense base because its revenue growth should have given it leverage on its fixed costs, resulting in better economies of scale and profitability. Its operating margin for the trailing 12 months was 35.7%.

Adobe Trailing 12-Month Operating Margin (GAAP)
Final Judgment

Adobe's business quality ultimately falls short of our standards. With its shares trailing the market in recent months, the stock trades at 3.4× forward price-to-sales (or $254.84 per share). This valuation multiple is fair, but we don't have much faith in the company. We're fairly confident there are better investments elsewhere. Let us point you toward a top digital advertising platform riding the creator economy.
